core_obligations: Reduce to a strictly perfect representative (proof lines 13696-13701): it suffices to check the map is an isomorphism locally on D, and by definition of a perfect object one may assume K is represented by a strictly perfect complex of O_D-modules.

Reduce to a finite complex of finite free modules (proof lines 13702-13705): the statement is additive in K, true for K_1 direct sum K_2 exactly when true for both summands, so one may assume K is a finite complex of finite free O_D-modules.

Reduce to a single free module (proof lines 13706-13710): a stupid truncation argument reduces to the case where K is a finite free O_D-module, and invariance under finite direct summands reduces further to K = O_D[n].
Conclude (proof lines 13710-13711): for K = O_D[n] the identity is trivially true, so the general case follows by the reductions.
proof_roadmap: Work locally so that the perfect object K is represented by a strictly perfect complex.
Use additivity to pass to a finite complex of finite free modules.
Use stupid truncations and summand-invariance to reduce to K = O_D[n].
The remaining case is trivial, and the reductions are reversible, so the projection formula holds for all perfect K.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the projection formula Rf_*E tensor^L K = Rf_*(E tensor^L Lf^*K) for a perfect coefficient object K (statement lines 13682-13693). The proof is a chain of explicit reductions rather than a computation: locality of the isomorphism makes K strictly perfect, additivity in K reduces to a finite complex of finite free modules, and a stupid-truncation argument together with invariance under finite direct summands reduces the statement to K = O_D[n], where it is trivial (proof lines 13696-13711). The non-formal content is the bookkeeping that each reduction is reversible, since the trivial case alone proves nothing. The claim is H2: a reduction chain, written out in full and using only standard permanence properties of perfect objects.
